content.title: About
content.content: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese made from cow's milk. Dry grated Parmesan is used as a flavorful topping, giving dishes a nutty, slightly sweet taste and a distinctive aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Parmesan holds a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) status and can only be produced in specific regions of Italy.
Grated Parmesan is a staple in Italian cuisine for sprinkling over pasta, risotto, and soups.
The cheese is aged a minimum of 12 months, often 24–36 months, which deepens its flavor.
Parmesan provides more than 30 % protein, making it a valuable source of protein.
Grated Parmesan stores well in an airtight container and retains its aroma for a long time.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Parmesan contains about 1,100 mg of calcium per 100 g, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Approximately 35 g of protein per 100 g helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains phosphorus and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for energy metabolism and immune function.

items.title: Low lactose
items.content: Extended aging reduces lactose levels, making Parmesan more tolerable for those with mild lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or milk proteins may react to Parmesan.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Grated Parmesan contains about 650 mg of sodium per 100 g, so those with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Approximately 430 kcal per 100 g, so consume in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sprinkle grated Parmesan over pasta, risotto, soups, salads, and casseroles. It can be added directly before serving or used as a fragrant base during cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry grated Parmesan in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from light. For longer storage keep it in the refrigerator, and for extended shelf life, in the freezer.
